# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 111 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 52 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_111_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 111

**1** Jesus said: "The heavens and the earth will be rolled up in your presence, and the one who lives from the Living One will not see death."

**2** Does not Jesus say: "Whoever finds himself — the world is not worthy of him?"

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** Saying 111 consists of two parts with a remarkable meta-structure: (1) An eschatological promise: cosmic dissolution + eternal life for those living from the Living One. (2) A rhetorical question appealing back to Jesus's own teaching ("Does not Jesus say...?") — the compiler or Thomas himself references Jesus's words as if reminding the reader.

**"Rolled up in your presence"** — *et ebe mpetophe*: the cosmic dissolution as a witnessed event — you will see it happen.

**"Lives from the Living One"** — *onkh ebol hitm petonkh*: drawing one's life from the source of life — a participatory ontology.

**"Whoever finds himself"** — the same self-finding theme of Sayings 56 and 80. Self-knowledge = transcendence of the world.

**Textual Note:** The meta-question ("Does not Jesus say...?") is unique in the gospel tradition — a moment of self-referential citation without parallel.
